package_info.why_malicious: The package is a trojanized version of the legitimate discord.js library, containing heavily obfuscated code that steals Discord authentication tokens and other sensitive data from local storage, exfiltrates them to attacker-controlled infrastructure, and in some variants provides remote access and command execution capabilities. This enables credential theft, account takeover, and full system compromise.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code iterates over browser and Discord client local storage folders, reads LevelDB files, extracts Discord authentication tokens using regular expressions, and sends the tokens along with the victim's public IP address to a hardcoded external server via HTTP POST, resulting in credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code accesses local storage folders associated with Discord and browsers, searches for token patterns using regex, and exfiltrates the results to an external server. This behavior is not present in legitimate libraries and is a clear sign of credential theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate discord.js library should not access or parse local storage files for tokens, nor transmit sensitive authentication data to external servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate software may access local storage for user settings, but never for extracting and exfiltrating authentication tokens.
key_indicators: Obfuscated code injected into a core library file
Enumeration of Discord and browser storage paths
Regex patterns matching Discord token formats
Network POST requests to hardcoded attacker-controlled domain (aba45cf.glitch.me)
Collection and exfiltration of public IP address

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code sends stolen Discord authentication tokens to a hardcoded Discord webhook endpoint via HTTP POST, enabling the attacker to receive credentials in real time.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Transmitting authentication tokens to a Discord webhook is a common exfiltration method used by malware targeting Discord users.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should never transmit user credentials or tokens to external webhooks or endpoints.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Webhooks are used for automation and notifications, but never for exfiltrating user credentials.
key_indicators: Hardcoded Discord webhook URL
POST request containing sensitive token data
Direct exfiltration of credentials to attacker infrastructure

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code uses an obfuscated eval-based loader to inject malicious JavaScript into the Discord client process, harvests sensitive user data including credentials, credit card information, and personally identifiable information (PII), and sends the stolen data to a hardcoded webhook endpoint, resulting in comprehensive data theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of obfuscated eval-based loaders to inject code into another application's process and exfiltrate sensitive data is a hallmark of infostealer malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not inject code into other applications, nor access or transmit user credentials, payment information, or PII.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate use case for code injection and credential theft in npm packages.
key_indicators: Obfuscated eval-based code loader
Code injection into Discord client process
Harvesting of credentials, credit cards, and PII
Exfiltration of stolen data to hardcoded webhook

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
// List of commands:
!webcampic - Takes a picture from the webcam
!screenshot - Takes the screenshot of the user's current screen
!vbs - Executes VBScript code received from the attacker
!Powershell - Executes PowerShell code received from the attacker
!clipboard - sends to the attacker content of the clipboard
!download - downloads file from the victim machine
!geolocated - send data from https://geolocation-db.com/json/
!passwords - sends to the attacker all passwords stored in a system
!shell - execute a shell command
!tokens - send to the attacker discord tokens
!listprocess - receive information about running processes
!startup - add a file to the startup
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, upon receiving attacker-issued commands via Discord chat, the code executes a wide range of remote access and data theft actions, including capturing webcam images, taking screenshots, executing arbitrary shell, VBScript, or PowerShell commands, stealing clipboard contents, downloading files, harvesting passwords and tokens, listing running processes, and establishing persistence by adding files to system startup.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code provides full remote access and control to an attacker, including the ability to execute arbitrary commands, capture sensitive data, and establish persistence, all of which are characteristic of remote access trojans (RATs).
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate npm package should provide remote shell, webcam access, credential theft, or persistence mechanisms without explicit user consent and transparency.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote administration tools exist, but not as hidden functionality in npm packages or without user knowledge and consent.
key_indicators: Obfuscated code with command handler logic
Support for a wide range of attacker-controlled commands
Integration with Discord chat for command and control (C2)
Capabilities for webcam, clipboard, shell, and credential access
Persistence mechanisms via startup file modification

execution_context.file_location: main package file (wafer-* family, octavius-public, mrg-message-broker)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, the code collects all environment variables from the running process, encodes them in base64, and sends them via HTTP POST to a hardcoded external server on pipedream.net, enabling the attacker to harvest secrets such as API keys and credentials from developer or CI/CD environments.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Harvesting and exfiltrating all environment variables is a common technique for stealing secrets, credentials, and API keys from compromised systems, especially in CI/CD or development environments.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages may collect limited telemetry, but should never exfiltrate full environment variables to external servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some telemetry or crash reporting tools may send limited environment information, but never the full set of environment variables or secrets.
key_indicators: Obfuscated code for exfiltration logic
Base64-encoded environment variable data
Hardcoded external exfiltration domain (a5eb7b362adc824ed7d98433d8eae80a.m.pipedream.net)
HTTP POST request containing sensitive environment data

attack_chain.action: User installs or imports the malicious npm package, often as a result of typosquatting or dependency confusion attacks.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is introduced and set up to execute within the victim's environment.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes at import-time or runtime, harvesting sensitive data such as Discord tokens, environment variables, credentials, and personally identifiable information (PII).
attack_chain.leads_to: Stolen data is collected and prepared for exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: The harvested data is exfiltrated to attacker-controlled infrastructure, including custom servers, Discord webhooks, and pipedream.net endpoints.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive data, enabling account takeover, further attacks, or resale of credentials.

attack_chain.action: For variants with remote access trojan (RAT) functionality, the attacker may issue further commands for remote control, data theft, persistence, or lateral movement.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full compromise of the victim system, including remote command execution and ongoing attacker access.

behavioral_signatures: Presence of obfuscated code in npm packages, especially in core library files or unexpected locations
Access to browser or Discord client local storage folders and LevelDB files
Use of regular expressions matching Discord token formats
Network requests to hardcoded external domains or Discord webhooks for data exfiltration
Exfiltration of environment variables or credentials, often base64-encoded
Presence of remote access or shell execution command handlers integrated with Discord chat
file_indicators: src/client/actions/UserGet.js containing obfuscated or injected code
eval(function(p,a,c,k,e,d)... patterns in main package files
References to Discord client storage paths (e.g., AppData/Roaming/Discord/Local Storage/leveldb)
Obfuscated code blocks in wafer-* or similar package families
network_indicators: Connections to geolocation-db.com/json/ for geolocation data
Unusual outbound traffic to domains not associated with legitimate package functionality
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm packages for the presence of obfuscated code, especially in files that should not contain such logic (e.g., core library files or main entry points). Flag packages that access browser or Discord client storage directories, use regular expressions to search for Discord token patterns, or exfiltrate data to hardcoded domains or Discord webhooks. Detect base64-encoded environment variable exfiltration and the presence of remote access command handlers, particularly those integrated with Discord chat. Use network monitoring to identify suspicious outbound HTTP POST requests to known exfiltration endpoints such as aba45cf.glitch.me, Discord webhooks, and pipedream.net domains. Correlate these behaviors to identify malicious packages and prevent credential and data theft.
